explicit_propositions.text: The speaker believes power should serve the majority rather than a privileged minority.

The speaker claims that lives of ordinary citizens are being sacrificed for systemic interests.
The speaker asserts that certain resources or rights belong inherently to all people.
The speaker argues that current systems have failed to deliver benefits to the public.
The speaker states that they are demanding accountability and change through organized resistance.
The speaker declares widespread participation in protests across multiple institutions.
The speaker insists that their movement is unified and resistant to division.
The speaker rejects the legitimacy of political and financial elites as deserving of trust or privilege.
The speaker vows continued pressure until demands are met, using persistent and coordinated tactics.

assumptions.text: The speaker assumes that collective action can effectively challenge entrenched power structures.
The speaker assumes that moral legitimacy lies with movements representing broad popular will.
The speaker assumes that symbolic and physical occupation of spaces undermines elite authority.
The speaker assumes that repetition and rhythm enhance persuasive force and unity within protest.
The speaker assumes that transparency and accountability are non-negotiable in governance.
The speaker assumes that existing institutions are corrupt or illegitimate and require replacement.
The speaker assumes that fear of sustained disruption will compel institutional change.
